prs.title: fix: validate PRM resource field per RFC 9728 Section 3.3
prs.author: bjoaquinc
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: PRM resource URL validation misfires: #1597 moves check_resource_allowed to _handle_protected_resource_response (validate at receive-time, RFC 9728 §3.3) and removes it from get_resource_url; #2590 adds _normalize_resource_url to strip trailing slashes before check_resource_allowed in get_resource_url — the exact code #1597 deletes. Both are triggered by cases where the PRM resource URL comparison produces wrong results, and they are technically incompatible: merging either makes the other a no-op or a merge conflict. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: PRM resource URL validation misfires: #1597 moves check_resource_allowed to _handle_protected_resource_response (validate at receive-time, RFC 9728 §3.3) and removes it from get_resource_url; #2590 adds _normalize_resource_url to strip trailing slashes before check_resource_allowed in get_resource_url — the exact code #1597 deletes. Both are triggered by cases where the PRM resource URL comparison produces wrong results, and they are technically incompatible: merging either makes the other a no-op or a merge conflict. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1597 addresses the architectural RFC 9728 §3.3 compliance issue — validation must occur when the metadata is received, not deferred to use-time — and its approach subsumes the problem #2590 tries to fix: once the resource field is validated at fetch-time before being stored, the get_resource_url path becomes a simple string conversion with no comparison needed. #2590 only adds URL normalization to a check that #1597 eliminates entirely, so its fix would be rendered dead code. URL normalization for trailing-slash edge cases can be incorporated into #1597's validation block if needed.

prs.title: fix: send notifications/cancelled on request timeout and caller cancellation
prs.author: dragogargo
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() incorrectly sent an error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec requirement that receivers must not send any response for a cancelled request. Both PRs modify the same lines in cancel() to remove that error-response send; merging one makes the other redundant and they would conflict. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() incorrectly sent an error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec requirement that receivers must not send any response for a cancelled request. Both PRs modify the same lines in cancel() to remove that error-response send; merging one makes the other redundant and they would conflict. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2514 is the more complete fix: it removes the incorrect error response (same as #2493) and additionally sends a spec-compliant CancelledNotification to the peer, which is the correct protocol behavior. PR #2493 only removes the error response and leaves no notification in its place, so #2514 addresses the full spec requirement while #2493 addresses only half of it.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe (refs #2431)
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Pickling MCPError subclasses (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) raises TypeError on unpickle because Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args) with (code, message, data) but the subclass constructor expects (elicitations, message=None). Both PRs target this same issue (#2431) in the same file. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Pickling MCPError subclasses (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) raises TypeError on unpickle because Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args) with (code, message, data) but the subclass constructor expects (elicitations, message=None). Both PRs target this same issue (#2431) in the same file. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2555 uses the standard __reduce__ protocol so pickle calls it automatically, explicitly references issue #2431, and includes test coverage in tests/shared/test_exceptions.py. PR #2478 adds a _restore_mcp_error helper but the visible diff contains no __reduce__ or __reduce_ex__ that wires it into the pickle protocol, leaving the fix incomplete.

clusters.pick_reason: #1597 addresses the architectural RFC 9728 §3.3 compliance issue — validation must occur when the metadata is received, not deferred to use-time — and its approach subsumes the problem #2590 tries to fix: once the resource field is validated at fetch-time before being stored, the get_resource_url path becomes a simple string conversion with no comparison needed. #2590 only adds URL normalization to a check that #1597 eliminates entirely, so its fix would be rendered dead code. URL normalization for trailing-slash edge cases can be incorporated into #1597's validation block if needed.

members.title: fix: validate PRM resource field per RFC 9728 Section 3.3
members.author: bjoaquinc
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: PRM resource URL validation misfires: #1597 moves check_resource_allowed to _handle_protected_resource_response (validate at receive-time, RFC 9728 §3.3) and removes it from get_resource_url; #2590 adds _normalize_resource_url to strip trailing slashes before check_resource_allowed in get_resource_url — the exact code #1597 deletes. Both are triggered by cases where the PRM resource URL comparison produces wrong results, and they are technically incompatible: merging either makes the other a no-op or a merge conflict. (2 PRs)
